app.title: Decomposing Humeral Orientation into Sub-Rotations
app.summary: A person opens a recorded motion trial, either by picking a subject and activity from a prepared catalogue or by uploading bone models, landmark files, a pose trajectory and its capture frequency. They scrub through the trial with a frame slider, or by hovering over curves of joint angles plotted across the trial, and fix one frame for close study. Up to three 3D panes then break that frame's bone orientation into its sub-rotations, each under a different decomposition convention. The person animates each sub-rotation step by step and switches between conventions in each pane, so they can see visually how the methods differ.

task.text: Explore a recorded joint motion and compare how different rotation-decomposition conventions describe the orientation of a bone at a chosen frame.

data.text: Motion trials sampled at a constant frequency. Each trial records the position and quaternion orientation of several rigid bodies over time, together with 3D surface models of the bones and anatomical landmark coordinates for each subject.
data.item: one frame of a motion trial: the pose of torso, scapula and humerus at one time sample

stage.text: analysing tracked bone motion after capture, comparing angle conventions

mechanism.text: A frame slider and line charts of decomposed angles over the trial drive three 3D panes. Hovering previews a frame, and clicking or the go arrow fixes it for decomposition. Each pane picks a decomposition convention and animates its sub-rotations step by step. The humerus panes share their camera, so rotating, panning or zooming one moves the others, and double-clicking a pane enlarges it.

field.text: Euler-angle and swing-twist decomposition of joint kinematics in shoulder biomechanics

workflow.name: break a recorded 3D orientation into component rotations under several conventions and compare them

steps.here: The folder icon opens a dialog to pick a subject and activity from a catalogue file. Manual File Selection instead takes bone surface models, landmark files, a pose trajectory and a capture frequency.

steps.step: move through time to find the moment of interest
steps.here: Dragging the top slider previews each capture frame in every 3D pane. Hovering along a plotted angle curve does the same.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The lower-right pane plots the decomposed angles across the whole trial. A dropdown switches between plane of elevation, angle of elevation, axial orientation, axial rotation and each decomposition sequence.
The downward arrow beside the slider, or a click on a plot point, fixes that frame and decomposes it in the 3D panes.

steps.step: step through the parts of a computation one at a time
steps.here: Numbered step buttons in each pane pick a sub-rotation. A play button and an animation bar then animate it until the moving bone overlaps the frame's true pose.

Each of three panes has its own dropdown of decomposition sequences, such as yx'y'', xz'y'', swing-twist and simultaneous for the humerus and yx'z'' for the scapula. Humerus panes share camera moves, and double-clicking enlarges a pane.

steps.step: change how the computation is set up
steps.here: Open Controls switches whether the humerus is measured against the torso or the scapula. It also toggles triads and arcs, earlier-step bones, body planes, an angle sketch, and the spherical area between the true and apparent paths of the distal humerus.

distinctive: The same orientation is broken down under several conventions, either as ordered sub-rotations or as one simultaneous rotation, so the person can see where the methods disagree.
Each sub-rotation is animated on a 3D bone model and ends overlapping the frame's true pose, which confirms that the decomposition is correct.
The reference body can be switched between the torso and the scapula, which changes both the decomposition and the plots.
A spherical area shows the gap between true and apparent axial rotation for the convention chosen.

parts.title: Trial selection dialog
parts.summary: Loads a motion trial by picking a subject and activity from a catalogue, or by uploading bone models, landmarks, a trajectory and a sampling frequency by hand.

parts.title: Capture frame slider
parts.summary: Scrubs through the trial's frames to preview them in every 3D pane, and a go arrow fixes the current frame for decomposition.

parts.title: Decomposition panes
parts.summary: Three 3D panes, each showing the bones decomposed under a convention chosen from its dropdown, with humerus cameras linked and a double-click to enlarge one pane.

parts.title: Sub-rotation step player
parts.summary: Lets the person pick a numbered sub-rotation and animate it with play and an animation bar, ending where the bone matches its true pose.

parts.title: Decomposed angle plots
parts.summary: Plots the chosen decomposition's angles over the whole trial. Hovering a curve previews that frame, and clicking it fixes the frame for the 3D panes.

parts.title: Controls panel
parts.summary: Sets the reference body for the humerus (torso or scapula) and toggles visual aids such as triads and arcs, earlier-step bones, body planes, angle sketches and the spherical area.

parts.title: Help overlay
parts.summary: Explains how to select a trial, choose a frame, read the views, animate sub-rotations and use the options.
